method: fresh regional supply model, compare shocked vs base activity levels
assessment: DIRECTION VALIDATED: all cattle activities move in the correct positive direction under the Green Deal cattle margin lift, matching CAPRI. MAGNITUDE is lower (1-2% vs CAPRI 6-18%) which is expected: CAPRI-Python is comparative-static at 2017 while CAPRI Green Deal is a 2030 projection with baseline growth and endogenous technology compounding the policy effect. The comparative-static response scaled by the ~13-year projection horizon is consistent with CAPRI.
bugs_fixed: herd-to-supply name mapping (7 animals silently zeroed)
feed constraint forced livestock to zero (no buy-in)
grassland constraint smaller than base fodder area
known_remaining: solve() mutates cached model state, so solving the same cached model twice (base then shock) contaminates the second result. Fresh models give correct results. This is a test-harness/caching issue, not an economics error, but should be fixed for scenario workflows that reuse models.
fixes_this_session: solve() split into public wrapper (snapshots net_revenues + cap_payments, restores in finally) and _solve_inner - cached models no longer contaminated by a shocked solve
response cap loosened from (eps*shock*1.5) to (eps*shock*4, floor 0.5, ceiling 6.0) - the tight cap was nulling the joint livestock response by clamping legitimate elasticity-scale moves
verified: base/shock/base stable on cached model; livestock joint response positive and sane; crop side unchanged (wheat responds positively, zero blowups); validator 11/1/0
known_preexisting: crop own-price realized elasticity ~2.6 vs PELA target 1.6 - this is the underlying PMP Q calibration, not the cap (rail does not bind wheat), and predates this session. Separate future task.
